Surah al-Furqan [Meccan, except verses 68, 69 and 70, which are Medinan; it has 77 verses and was revealed after Surah Ya-Sin]

﴿Blessed is He﴾ (Exalted is He), ﴿who sent down the Criterion﴾ (al-Furqan), meaning the Qur'an, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, ﴿upon His servant﴾ Muhammad, ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾, meaning to mankind and the jinn, not the angels, ﴿a warner﴾ (mukhawwifan), frightening them of the punishment of Allah.

﴿He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, who has no partner in the dominion, and who created everything and determined it precisely﴾ [i.e., everything that is suited to be created]. ﴿Then determined it precisely﴾ [i.e., He proportioned it, shaping it with due proportion].

The Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 25, verse 3:

﴿And they have taken,﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿besides Him,﴾ i.e., besides Allah, i.e., other than Him, ﴿gods,﴾ which are the idols, ﴿who create nothing, while they are themselves created, and possess not for themselves any harm﴾ i.e., warding it off, ﴿nor any benefit﴾ i.e., bringing it about, ﴿and possess not death, nor life﴾ i.e., causing death to anyone or giving life to anyone, ﴿nor resurrection﴾ i.e., raising of the dead.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 4:

﴿And those who disbelieved said: "This is nothing but a fabrication﴾, i.e., the Qur'an is nothing but ﴿a falsehood﴾, a lie, ﴿which he (Muhammad) has invented, and others have helped him with it﴾, and they are ﴿people from among the People of the Scripture﴾. ﴿So they have come with injustice and falsehood﴾, disbelief and lying; i.e., they have come with both of them.

"And they said" also: it is "legends of the former peoples" (asatir al-awwalin), their falsehoods. Usturah (plural: asatir) is with a damma. "He has had them written down" (iktatabaha): he had them copied from those people by someone else. "So they are dictated" (fa-hiya tumla): they are read out "to him" (alayhi), so that he may memorize them, "in the morning and the evening" (bukratan wa-asilan): at dawn and at dusk. Allah the Exalted said, in refutation of them:
﴿Say: "It was sent down by the One who knows the secret" (al-sirr), meaning the unseen (al-ghayb), "in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving" to the believers, "Merciful" to them﴾

﴿And they say, "What is this Messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why has not an angel been sent down to him, so that he would be with him as a warner"﴾ "Why not" (*halla*, a variant of *lawla*) "has an angel been sent down to him" "to confirm him" (*yuṣaddiquhu*).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 8:

﴿Or a treasure be cast down to him from the heaven﴾, so that he may spend from it and not need to walk in the markets seeking a livelihood. ﴿Or he have a garden﴾, an orchard, ﴿from which he may eat﴾, i.e., from its fruits, and so be content with it. In another reading, "we eat" (naʾkulu) with the nun: i.e., we, so that he would have a superiority over us through it. ﴿And the wrongdoers said﴾, i.e., the disbelievers said to the believers, ﴿You follow but a man bewitched﴾, deceived, his intellect overcome.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 9:

﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you﴾ by [calling you] the one bewitched and needy of what he spends, and [saying he needs] an angel to act together with him in the matter; ﴿so they have gone astray﴾ by that from the guidance; ﴿and they cannot find a way﴾, a path, to it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 10:

﴿Blessed is He﴾ (tabaraka) increased in goodness, ﴿who, if He wills, will give you better than that﴾, than what they said of the treasure and the garden, ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, i.e., in this world, because He willed to give it to him in the Hereafter. ﴿And will assign for you﴾ with the jussive (bi-l-jazm) ﴿palaces﴾ as well. In another reading it is in the nominative (bi-l-raf') as a resumptive new clause (isti'naf).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 25, verse 11:

﴿Nay, they denied the Hour﴾ (al-Sa'a), the Resurrection; ﴿and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire﴾ (sa'iran), a fire kindled (musa"ara), i.e., intensely heated.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 25, verse 12:

﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring.﴾ (Its) boiling, like the angry person when his chest boils with anger. And roaring: a intense sound. Or the hearing of the raging is its seeing them and its knowledge of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 13:

﴿And when they are thrown into it, into a narrow place therein, shackled together,﴾ with the doubled and the single letter (in the reading of "ألقوا" and "ضيقا" as variants), meaning that it will be constricted upon them. The word "minha" (from it) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) relating to "makānan" (a place), because it is originally an attribute (ṣifah) of it. ﴿shackled together﴾ means bound in fetters, having been made to be joined (qurrinat), i.e., their hands were gathered up to their necks in the chains, and the doubling of the letter is for intensification (li-l-takthīr). ﴿There they will cry out for destruction﴾, meaning ruin, and it will be said to them:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 14:

﴿Do not call out for one destruction today, but call out for many destructions.﴾ Like your punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 15:

﴿Say: Is that better, or the Garden of eternity which has been promised to the God-fearing?﴾ That is, the aforementioned threat and the description of the Fire. ﴿It shall be for them a reward﴾ [i.e., a recompense, a thawab] ﴿and a destination﴾ [i.e., a place of return], ﴿in His knowledge, may He be exalted﴾ [kanat lahum: it was, in His knowledge, for them].

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding eternally﴾: this is a necessary state (ḥāl lāzimah). ﴿Kāna﴾ (it was): their promise was what has been mentioned. ﴿A promise binding upon your Lord, one to be asked for﴾: the one who was promised it asks Him for it. Or the angels ask Him on their behalf: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eternity which You promised them﴾. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 25, verse 17:

﴿And on the Day He gathers them﴾ with the nūn (the first-person plural reading, نُحْشِرُهُمْ) and the taḥtāniyya (the third-person reading with the yā', يَحْشُرُهُمْ, as "He gathers"). ﴿and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾, that is, other than Him, from among the angels, ʿĪsā, ʿUzayr and the jinn. ﴿Then He will say﴾, exalted is He, with the taḥtāniyya and the nūn (فَيَقُولُ and فَنَقُولُ), addressed to those who were worshipped, to establish the proof against those who worshipped them. ﴿"Did you﴾ with the two hamzas realized (أَأَنْتُمْ, both hamzas pronounced in full), with the second hamza changed to an alif, with it eased (softened), with an alif inserted between the eased hamza and the other, and with that alif omitted. ﴿lead these servants of Mine astray?"﴾ Did you cause them to fall into error by your command to them to worship you? ﴿Or did they themselves stray from the way﴾ the path of truth, of their own accord?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 18:

﴿They said: Glory be to You!﴾ (declaring You far above what is not befitting to You) ﴿It was not for us to take any protectors (awliya') apart from You﴾ (i.e., other than You). The word "min" (from) here is extra (ziyadah), serving to emphasize the negation; "awliya'" is the first object (maf'ul awwal), and what precedes it ("min dunika," apart from You) is the second object. So how could we command that they worship us? ﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment﴾ (before them) by lengthening their lifespans and widening their provision ﴿until they forgot the Reminder﴾ (they abandoned the admonition and faith in the Qur'an) ﴿and they were a people doomed﴾ (lost, perishing).

**﴿So they have denied you in what you say﴾**, i.e., the things that were worshipped (*al-ma'budun*) denied the worshippers (*al-'abidin*) in what you say, namely that they are gods. The verb **تَقُولُونَ** (*taqulun*) is read with the *fawqaniyya* (the upper-dotted *ta'*), meaning "you say," addressed to the worshippers.

**﴿So they are not able﴾**, read with the *tahtaniyya* (the lower-dotted *ya'*) and with the *fawqaniyya* (the upper-dotted *ta'*). **فَما يَسْتَطِيعُونَ** (*fa-ma yastati'un*) with the *ya'* means "they are not able," referring to the worshipped things, and with the *ta'* means "you are not able," referring to the worshippers. I.e., neither they nor you are able **﴿to avert﴾** (*sarfan*), meaning to repel **﴿the punishment from you﴾**, **﴿nor to help﴾** (*nasran*), meaning to prevent you from it.

**﴿And whoever among you does wrong﴾**, i.e., associates partners with God (*yushrik*), **﴿We will make him taste a great punishment﴾**, i.e., a severe one in the Hereafter.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn, a tafsir, or Qur'anic commentary) on surah 25, verse 20:**

﴿We did not send any messengers before you except that they surely ate food and walked in the markets.﴾ So you are like them in that, and it has been said to them what has been said to you. ﴿And We have made some of you a trial (fitnah) for others﴾, meaning a affliction by which the rich is tested by the poor, the healthy by the sick, and the noble by the lowly. The second says in each case: "Why am I not like the first in each?" ﴿Will you be patient?﴾ over what you hear from those by whom you have been tested. This is a question with the meaning of a command: that is, be patient. ﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ of whoever is patient and whoever is impatient.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 21:

﴿And those who do not hope for Our meeting say﴾ — i.e., who do not fear the Resurrection (al-ba'th) — ﴿"Why not (lawla)" (halla) ﴿have the angels been sent down to us﴾ so that they would be messengers to us, ﴿or we see our Lord﴾ so that we would be told that Muhammad is His messenger?﴾ ﴿Indeed they have become arrogant﴾ (takabbaru) ﴿concerning﴾ (sha'n) ﴿their own selves, and they have transgressed﴾ (taghaw) ﴿with a great transgression﴾ — by their demand to see Allah Most High in this world. And "wa'taw" (وَعَتَوْا) with the waw, according to its original form, unlike "ataa" (عِتِيّ) with substitution in Maryam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 22:

﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾ among the rest of the creatures, that is the Day of Resurrection, and its being in the accusative is by an implied "remember" (udhkur). ﴿there will be no good news that Day for the criminals﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, unlike the believers, for they will have the good news of Paradise. ﴿And they will say, "A forbidding, forbidden [barrier]!"﴾ as was their custom in the world when a hardship befell them; i.e., they will seek refuge, saying "ʿawdhan maʿadha," seeking protection from the angels.

ﷻ "And We will turn to what they did of deeds" — (Allah says) We will proceed to (qadimna = "We will intend/attend to") what they did of deeds, of good such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, hospitality to guests, and relieving the distressed, in the world; ﴿So We will make it scattered dust⦆... 

Let me give the translation cleanly:

"And We will turn to what they did of deeds" (qadimna: We will intend/proceed to) — "what they did of deeds," of good, such as charity, maintaining ties of kinship, hospitality to guests, and relieving the oppressed in the world. ﴿And We will make it scattered dust⦆ — it is what is seen in the rays of the sun coming through the openings (al-kuwa, windows) upon which the sun shines, like scattered dust; that is, it is like it in having no benefit, since there is no reward for it due to the lack of its required condition, and they are recompensed for it in the world.

﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day﴾, the Day of Resurrection, ﴿are better in abode﴾ than the disbelievers in the world, ﴿and better in resting place﴾ than them. That is, a place of *qaylula* (the midday rest taken at noon in the heat). From this was taken the ending of the reckoning at midday, as is related in a hadith

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 25:

﴿And the day the sky is split open﴾, i.e., every sky, ﴿with the clouds﴾, i.e., together with it, and it is white cloud, ﴿and the angels will be sent down﴾ from every sky, ﴿in a descent﴾. It is the Day of Resurrection, and its accusative (naṣb) is by an implied verb, "remember" (udhkur). In another reading it is read with the shin of tashaqqaqa doubled (tashshaqqaqa), with the second tā' assimilated into it, as it originally is; and in another reading: nunazzilu, with two nūns, the second one sukūn, the lām with ḍamma, and al-malā'ikata in the accusative.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 26:

﴿The sovereignty on that Day will be truly for the Most Merciful﴾ (none shares it with Him), ﴿and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers﴾, unlike the believers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 27:

﴿And on the Day the wrongdoer bites his hands﴾ — the polytheist, namely ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, who had pronounced the two testimonies (shahadatayn) and then reverted to unbelief to please Ubayy ibn Khalaf. ﴿Upon his hands﴾ out of regret and anguish on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿He will say: "Oh!"﴾ — (yā here is) for calling attention. ﴿"Would that I had taken a way (sabil) along with the Messenger"﴾ — Muhammad (ﷺ) — ﴿"a way"﴾, meaning a path to guidance.

﴿Ya waylata﴾: its alif is a substitute for the possessive ya' (ya' al-idafa), meaning "ya waylatī" (O my destruction). Its meaning is "my ruin" (halakatī).
﴿Would that I had not taken so-and-so﴾: i.e., Ubayy.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 29:

﴿He has indeed led me astray from the Reminder﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿after it had come to me﴾, by turning me away from believing in it. ﴿And Satan is ever a deserter of man﴾, the disbeliever, by abandoning him and disowning him at the time of trial.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 30:

﴿And the Messenger says﴾ Muhammad, ﴿"O my Lord, indeed my people﴾ Quraysh ﴿have taken this Qur'an as deserted"﴾ abandoned, left aside.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 31:

﴿And thus﴾ as We have made for you an enemy from among the polytheists of your people, ﴿We have made for every prophet﴾ before you ﴿an enemy from among the criminals﴾, the polytheists. So be patient as they were patient. ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as a guide﴾ for you ﴿and a helper﴾, one who helps you against your enemies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 32:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ (Lawla: "Why not?" — meaning hallā, "would that," in the sense of "why not") ﴿sent down to him all at once﴾ like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms. God the Exalted says: We sent it down ﴿thus﴾ in parts, ﴿so that We may strengthen your heart with it﴾, i.e., strengthen your heart, ﴿and We have recited it in a measured recitation﴾, i.e., We brought it piece by piece, gradually and deliberately, to facilitate its understanding and its memorization.
﴿And they do not bring you any example﴾ to nullify your affair, ﴿except that We bring you the truth﴾ that repels it, ﴿and a better explanation﴾ (tafsīran), a clearer exposition.

Those are the ones who will be gathered on their faces (﴿الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوههمْ﴾), that is, they will be driven, (﴿إلى جَهَنَّم﴾) to Hell. (﴿أُولَئِكَ شَرّ مَكانًا﴾) That is, Hell is the worse place, (﴿وأَضَلّ سَبِيلًا﴾) and further astray in the way, that is, they went further wrong than others, and that is their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 35:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ the Torah ﴿and made his brother Aaron with him a minister﴾ a helper.

"In" here is the light (mukhaffafah) form of the heavy "inna", and its subject is omitted: meaning, "Indeed he" (innahu) "almost misled us" (kada layudilluna), i.e., turned us away "from our gods" (ʿan ālihatina), "had we not been patient in adhering to them" (law-la an ṣabarnā ʿalayhā), he would have turned us away from them. The singular of the first is nashur, like rasul, and of the last is bashir. ﴿And We send down from the sky water that is pure﴾, purifying (mutahhiran).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 49:

﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾ (read as li-nuḥyiya with the lightened form, bi-l-takhfif, in which the masculine and feminine are alike; he (God) used the masculine (dhakarahu) in view of the place (bi-i'tibar al-makan)) ﴿and give drink to﴾ it, i.e., the water, ﴿of what We have created: cattle [anʿaman], camels, cows and sheep, and many humans [anasiyya kathiran]﴾ (the plural of insan, whose original form was anasin, then the nun was replaced by a yā' and the yā' was assimilated into it; or it is the plural of insiyy).

And certainly We have distributed it among them (i.e., the water) so that they may remember (ليذكروا), its original form being يَتَذَكَّرُوا (yatadhakkaru), with the taa' assimilated into the dhaal. In another reading it is ليَذْكُرُوا (liyadhkuru), with the dhaal sukun and the kaaf dammah: i.e., the blessing of Allah in it. But most of the people refused except denial (كُفُورًا, kufuran), obstinately rejecting the blessing, when they said: "We were given rain by such-and-such a star-rising (nawʾ)."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 51:

﴿And had We willed, We would have sent into every town a warner.﴾ He would warn its people. But We have sent you to the people of all the towns as a warner, so that your reward may be great.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 52:**

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers﴾ in what they desire, ﴿and strive against them with it﴾, i.e., with the Qur'an.

﴿And it is He who let the two seas loose﴾: He sent them flowing side by side. ﴿This one is sweet, very sweet and fresh﴾, and ﴿this one is salty, very salty and bitter﴾. ﴿And He placed between them a barrier﴾, a partition that prevents one from mixing with the other, ﴿and a forbidden partition﴾, a screen by which their mixing is prevented.

And He it is who created from water a human being, and made him [a person with] lineage and marriage relations. Your Lord is ever Competent.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: ﴿And He it is who created from water a human being﴾ from the seminal fluid (al-mani), a human being. ﴿and made him [a person with] lineage﴾ possessing lineage ﴿and marriage relations﴾ possessing marriage relations, by his marrying, whether male or female, seeking procreation. ﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾ capable of whatever He wills.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 55:

﴿And they worship﴾ i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿besides Allah that which neither benefits them﴾ by worshipping it ﴿nor harms them﴾ by abandoning it, namely the idols. ﴿And the disbeliever is ever a helper﴾ an aide ﴿against his Lord﴾ to Satan by obeying him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 56:

﴿And We have not sent you (O Muhammad) except as a bringer of good tidings﴾ of Paradise ﴿and a warner﴾ frightening [people] from the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 57:

﴿Say, "I do not ask you any wage for it"﴾ i.e., for conveying what I have been sent with, ﴿except﴾ but ﴿for whoever wills to take to his Lord a way﴾ a path, by spending of his wealth in seeking His pleasure, exalted is He; so I do not prevent him from that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 58:

﴿And put your trust in the Ever-Living, who does not die, and glorify Him, praising Him﴾ (mutalabbisan, i.e., joined) ﴿with His praise﴾, meaning: say, "Glory be to God, and praise be to God." ﴿And sufficient is He as one who is Acquainted with the sins of His servants﴾, Aware (khabiran, i.e., "Acquainted" or "Aware"), and "with" (bi) is connected to "sins" (bi-dhunubin).

He it is who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days — of the days of this world; that is, in their measure, for there was then no sun. Had He willed, He could have created them in a blink of an eye, but He deferred it in order to teach His creation deliberateness (al-tathabbut).

Then He established Himself upon the Throne (al-'arsh) — which, linguistically, is the seat of sovereignty — the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) being a substitute (badal) for the pronoun in "established" (istawa): that is, an establishment befitting Him.

So ask about Him (fas'al bihi), O human being, of one who is informed (khabiran), who will inform you of His attributes.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 60:

﴿And when it is said to them﴾ to the disbelievers of Makkah, ﴿"Prostrate yourselves to the Most Merciful"﴾ they say, ﴿"And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾ with the second person in the feminine and the masculine forms (taʾmuruna in both the upper and lower readings), and the one who commands is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"and we do not know Him?"﴾ No! ﴿And it increases them﴾ this saying to them ﴿in aversion﴾ from faith.

﴿Blessed﴾ means exalted in greatness, ﴿is He who placed in the sky buruj﴾ (constellations, or zodiacal mansions), ﴿twelve﴾: al-Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawza' (Gemini), al-Saratan (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mizan (Libra), al-Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jady (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius), and al-Hut (Pisces). They are the mansions (manazil) of the seven wandering planets (sayyara): Mars (al-Mirrikh) has Aries and Scorpio; Venus (al-Zuhra) has Taurus and Libra; Mercury (Utarid) has Gemini and Virgo; the Moon (al-Qamar) has Cancer; the Sun (al-Shams) has Leo; Jupiter (al-Mushtari) has Sagittarius and Pisces; and Saturn (Zuhal) has Capricorn and Aquarius. ﴿And placed therein﴾ also ﴿a lamp (siraj)﴾, which is the Sun, ﴿and a luminous moon﴾. In one reading, the word is surujan in the plural, meaning nayyirat (shining bodies). The Moon was singled out for mention from among them because of a particular kind of excellence.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 62:

﴿And it is He who made the night and the day succeed each other﴾, i.e., each of them replaces the other, ﴿for whoever wishes to remember﴾ (with the doubled and the single letter, as mentioned earlier), i.e., what he missed in one of them of good, so that he may do it in the other, ﴿or wishes to be grateful﴾, i.e., to give thanks for the blessing of his Lord upon him in both of them.

"And the servants of the Most Merciful" is the subject (mubtada'), and what follows are its attributes (sifat), up to "those will be rewarded" (ula'ika yujzawna), with nothing intervening in it that is objectionable: "who walk upon the earth in humility" (hawnan), i.e., with tranquility (bi-sakinah) and humbleness (tawadu'). "And when the ignorant address them" with what they dislike, "they say, 'Peace'" (salaman), i.e., a speech by which they are safe from sin (al-ithm).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 64:

﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾ (sujjadan) is the plural of sajid (one who prostrates), and (qiyaman) means standing, i.e., they pray during the night.
And those who say, ﴿Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever-clinging﴾ (that is, constant, inescapable).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 66:

﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ "Evil" (بِئْسَ, bi'sa): "how wretched," the verb of dispraise. "Settlement and residence" (مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقامًا): it means a place of staying and dwelling.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 67:

﴿And those who, when they spend,﴾ on their dependents, ﴿do not waste nor are niggardly﴾ — with the first letter of the verb pronounced with a fatha or a damma: i.e., they do not restrict [their spending]. ﴿And their spending was between that﴾ — the wastefulness (al-israf) and the niggardliness (al-iqtar) — ﴿a means﴾, a moderate course.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 25, verse 68:

﴿And those who do not invoke another god alongside Allah, nor kill the soul which Allah has forbidden⁠ ⁠— killing it⁠ ⁠— ﴿except by right﴾, nor commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever does that⁠ ⁠— i.e., one of the three⁠ ⁠— ﴿will meet a penalty﴾, i.e., a punishment.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 25, verse 69:

﴿Yudā'af﴾ (the punishment will be doubled for him). In another reading, it is ﴿yuḍa''af﴾ with the shadda (gemination of the ʿayn), ﴿for him the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide in it﴾ forever, with both verbs in the jussive (majzūm) as substitutions (badal), and in the nominative (marfūʿ) as a new independent clause (istiʾnāf). ﴿Humiliated﴾ (muhānan) is a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 70:

﴿Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ from among them, ﴿then those—Allah will change their evil deeds﴾ mentioned [earlier] ﴿into good deeds﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 25, verse 71:

﴿And whoever repents﴾ from his sins, other than those mentioned, ﴿and does righteous deeds, then indeed he turns back to Allah with a turning back﴾, meaning he returns to Him with a return, so He rewards him with good.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 25, verse 72:

﴿And those who do not bear witness to falsehood﴾ i.e., lying and falsehood. ﴿And when they pass by vain talk﴾ of foul speech and other things, ﴿they pass by with dignity﴾ turning away from it.

﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the signs of their Lord﴾ are admonished by ﴿the signs of their Lord﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ do not fall down (yasquutu) upon them, ﴿rather they fall down﴾ hearing, seeing, and benefiting.

﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from among our spouses and our offspring"﴾ (read in both the plural and the singular) ﴿a comfort of the eyes﴾ for us, by seeing them obedient to You; ﴿and make us a leader for the righteous﴾ in goodness.

﴿Those will be rewarded with the lofty chamber﴾: the high rank in Paradise, ﴿for what they endured﴾ in obedience to God. ﴿They will be met﴾ (*wa-yulaqqawna*, recited with the doubling of the letter *lām* (*tashdīd*) and without it (*takhfīf*), with the *yā'* vowelled with a *fatḥah*) ﴿therein﴾, in the chamber, ﴿with greeting and peace﴾ from the angels.

﴿Abiding therein; excellent is it as a place of settlement and residence.﴾ (It is) a place of residence for them. "Those" (ulaika) and what follows it is the predicate (khabar, the part of a nominal sentence that completes the meaning) of "the servants of the Most Merciful" (ibad al-Rahman), which is the subject (mubtada', the topic of the nominal sentence).

Say (O Muhammad) to the people of Makkah: "My Lord would not care for you (ma here is negating) were it not for your supplication (to Him) in times of hardship, whereby He would remove it. So indeed (fa-qad, meaning: then how would He care for you) when you have denied (the Messenger and the Qur'an). So the punishment will be inevitable (lizaman), constantly attaching to you in the Hereafter after it has befallen you in this world; thus seventy of them were killed on the Day of Badr." The answer to "lawla" (were it not for) is what is indicated by what precedes it.
